reviewMethod: Antigravity drafts separately reviewed against complete archived version bodies and source notes; source discrepancies retained explicitly.

headings.title: Definition of aquaculture for this section
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1995 S.B. 109 § 1). Defines "aquaculture" solely for section 277.024 as the controlled propagation, growth, and harvest of aquatic organisms as defined by rule of the conservation commission. Separate review (antigravity_reviewer_r32): Retained drafted title after reading complete archived subsection text and notes.

headings.title: Classification of aquaculture products as livestock
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note (L. 1995 S.B. 109 § 1). Directs that aquatic products obtained through aquaculture be treated and classified as livestock when construing any Missouri law or rule or regulation of any state department, board, or commission. Separate review (antigravity_reviewer_r32): Retained drafted title after reading complete archived subsection text and notes.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived text of subsections 1–2 and history note (L. 1995 S.B. 109 § 1); verified all fingerprints. Confirmed section-specific definition of "aquaculture" referencing conservation commission rules and classification of aquaculture aquatic products as livestock across Missouri laws and agency rules. Both drafted titles retained.

headings.title: License application contents and separate-location requirement
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1943 p. 310 § 4, A. 1949 S.B. 1100, A.L. 1957 p. 20, A.L. 1989 S.B. 300, A.L. 2015 S.B. 12). Requires persons establishing or operating a livestock sale or market to file an application with the state veterinarian stating business nature, city, township, county, post office address, and required information, with a separate license for each sale location. Separate review (antigravity_reviewer_r32): Retained drafted title after reading complete archived subsection text and notes.

headings.title: License issuance, annual fee, and license year
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Directs the state veterinarian to issue a license upon payment of an annual fee fixed by rule or regulation, authorizing operation for the license year or unexpired portion unless revoked. Separate review (antigravity_reviewer_r32): Retained drafted title after reading complete archived subsection text and notes.

headings.title: Fee revenue cap and Livestock Sales and Markets Fees Fund
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Caps chapter 277 license fee revenue at the total cost of administering the chapter for the ensuing year, creates the Livestock Sales and Markets Fees Fund (noting plural "Markets" here versus singular "market" in 277.050(3)), and dedicates deposits subject to appropriation to the animal health division. Separate review (antigravity_reviewer_r32): Retained drafted title after reading complete archived subsection text and notes.

headings.title: Five-year licensing bar after prior revocation violation
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note. Prohibits issuing a livestock market license to any proprietorship, partnership, or corporation if a proprietor, partner, officer, or major shareholder participated in a chapter 277 violation within the preceding five years that resulted in license revocation. Separate review (antigravity_reviewer_r32): Retained drafted title after reading complete archived subsection text and notes.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived text of subsections 1–4 and history note (through 2015 S.B. 12); verified all fingerprints. Confirmed state veterinarian application details, per-location licensing, rule-fixed annual fee, administrative-cost revenue cap, creation of the "Livestock Sales and Markets Fees Fund" (plural "Markets", contrasted with singular "market" in 277.050(3)), and 5-year post-revocation licensing bar for entities with participating principals. All 4 drafted titles retained.

headings.title: Grounds and hearing procedure for license suspension or revocation
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 including subdivisions (1)-(7) and history/effective-date notes (L. 1943 p. 310 § 5, A.L. 1957 p. 20, A.L. 1989 S.B. 300; effective 5-04-89). Authorizes the director or designated representative, after at least 10 days' notice with full charges and a public hearing, to suspend or revoke a license on seven enumerated grounds (false statements/fraud, diseased or stolen animals, sanitation failures, recordkeeping/production failures, bond/insolvency/payment failures, state veterinarian rule violations, or state/federal animal health law violations), subject to subsection 2 appeal. Separate review (antigravity_reviewer_r32): Retained drafted title after reading complete archived subsection text and notes.

headings.title: Chapter 536 review of license sanctions and civil penalties
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history/effective-date notes. Permits a licensee to apply for review under chapter 536 of any director order suspending or revoking a license or imposing a civil penalty. Separate review (antigravity_reviewer_r32): Retained drafted title after reading complete archived subsection text and notes. Verified chapter 536 review text expressly names "The licensee" for suspension, revocation, or civil penalty orders.

headings.title: Corrective notice, informal hearings, and civil penalties
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history/effective-date notes. Provides certified-letter notice and state veterinarian informal hearing for facility sanitation/structural, record-form, or sale-procedure violations before proceeding under subsection 1, authorizes civil penalties up to $1,000 per violation after public hearing against licensees and conspiring third parties where lesser action is warranted, and directs deposits to the "livestock sales and market fees fund" (singular "market" in archived text, compared to "Markets" in 277.040(3)). Separate review (antigravity_reviewer_r32): Retained drafted title after reading complete archived subsection text and notes. Verified archived singular fund name "livestock sales and market fees fund" (versus plural "Markets" in 277.040(3)) and 5-04-89 effective date.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived text of subsections 1–3 (including subdivisions (1)–(7) of sub 1) and history/effective-date notes (effective 5-04-89); verified all fingerprints. Confirmed 10-day notice and public hearing on seven suspension/revocation grounds, chapter 536 review expressly available to the licensee, certified-letter corrective notice/informal hearing for facility/record/sale issues, civil penalties up to $1,000 against licensees and conspiring third parties, and archived singular fund name "livestock sales and market fees fund" (versus plural "Markets" in 277.040(3)). All 3 drafted titles retained.

headings.title: Licensee responsibility for net proceeds and safe delivery
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1943 p. 310 § 7, A.L. 1957 p. 20). Makes each licensee responsible to the consignor for the net proceeds of any bona fide livestock sale and responsible on the sale date to the purchaser for safe delivery of the animal in a loading chute at the sale site. Separate review (antigravity_reviewer_r32): Revised "liability" to "responsibility" to match the statutory wording ("is responsible to") and avoid implying extra-statutory tort liability. (Prior draft: "Licensee liability for net proceeds and safe delivery".)

headings.title: Definition of net proceeds
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note (L. 1943 p. 310 § 7, A.L. 1957 p. 20). Defines "net proceeds" as the sale amount remaining after deducting commissions, inspection fees, and other deductible items authorized by the sale terms announced at the opening of the livestock sale. Separate review (antigravity_reviewer_r32): Retained drafted title after reading complete archived subsection text and notes.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived text of subsections 1–2 and history note (through 1957 p. 20); verified all fingerprints. Confirmed consignor net-proceeds duty, sale-date purchaser loading-chute safe-delivery duty, and announced-sale-terms definition of "net proceeds". Revised sub 1 title from "liability" to "responsibility" to match exact statutory phrasing; retained sub 2.

headings.title: Pre-licensing bond requirement
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history/effective-date notes (L. 1943 p. 310 § 8, A.L. 1957 p. 20, A.L. 1978 H.B. 1634, A.L. 1989 S.B. 300; effective 5-04-89). Requires every person subject to chapter 277 to provide a satisfactory bond in an amount designated by the state veterinarian before receiving a license. Separate review (antigravity_reviewer_r32): Retained drafted title after reading complete archived subsection text and notes.

headings.title: Alternative financial security, bank review, and trust agreements
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history/effective-date notes. Allows substituting FDIC- or FSLIC-insured certificates of deposit (retaining archived "federal savings and loan insurance corporation" name), bank irrevocable letters of credit, or USDA Packers and Stockyards Administration-approved security for the subsection 1 bond; governs beneficiary/form rules, director refusal and division of finance evaluation of issuing banks, and trust agreements naming the state veterinarian as letter-of-credit trustee. Separate review (antigravity_reviewer_r32): Retained drafted title after reading complete archived subsection text and notes. Verified archived institutional names "federal savings and loan insurance corporation" and "Packers and Stockyards Administration" / "Packers and Stockyards Administration Act"; retained without modernization.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived text of subsections 1–2 and history/effective-date notes (effective 5-04-89); verified all fingerprints. Confirmed state-veterinarian-designated pre-licensing bond, substitute FDIC/FSLIC CDs, bank irrevocable letters of credit, and USDA Packers and Stockyards Administration security (retaining archived agency/statute names without modernization), bank insolvency refusal/division of finance cooperation, and trust-agreement state veterinarian trustee role. Both drafted titles retained.

headings.title: Mandatory inspection of livestock offered for sale
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history/effective-date notes (L. 1943 p. 310 § 10, A.L. 1957 p. 20, A.L. 1989 S.B. 300; effective 5-04-89). Directs the state veterinarian to require all chapter 277 licensees to obtain inspection of all livestock offered for sale at any livestock sale or market in the designated manner. Separate review (antigravity_reviewer_r32): Retained drafted title after reading complete archived subsection text and notes.

headings.title: Discretionary vaccination or quarantine orders and limit
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history/effective-date notes. Authorizes the state veterinarian or deputy to order livestock vaccinated, quarantined, or both when advisable, while prohibiting a general order requiring vaccination of all livestock sold in the state or at all livestock sales. Separate review (antigravity_reviewer_r32): Retained drafted title after reading complete archived subsection text and notes.

headings.title: Approved inspectors, state dismissal, and operator dismissal requests
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history/effective-date notes. Requires inspections and official disease tests/identification by a licensed veterinarian or state-veterinarian-approved person under rules, permits dismissal by the state veterinarian for neglect or misconduct, and establishes review, hearing, and 30-day approval-withdrawal procedures for market operator dismissal requests unless the predominant reason is refusal to breach state or federal testing/inspection requirements. Separate review (antigravity_reviewer_r32): Retained drafted title after reading complete archived subsection text and notes.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived text of subsections 1–3 and history/effective-date notes (effective 5-04-89); verified all fingerprints. Confirmed mandatory inspection of livestock offered for sale, discretionary vaccination/quarantine authority with explicit statewide general-vaccination prohibition, approved veterinary inspectors, state dismissal for neglect/misconduct, and 30-day market-operator dismissal review with compliance-refusal exception. All 3 drafted titles retained.

headings.title: Class E felony for offering bribes to operators or market veterinarians
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history/effective-date notes (L. 1989 S.B. 300 §§ 277.180, 277.200, A.L. 2014 S.B. 491; effective 1-01-17). Makes offering a bribe to any livestock market or sale operator or market veterinarian to induce a chapter 277 violation a class E felony. Separate review (antigravity_reviewer_r32): Revised "bribing" to "offering bribes to" to match the statutory conduct ("offers a bribe") without requiring acceptance. (Prior draft: "Class E felony for bribing operators or market veterinarians".)

headings.title: No private cause of action created by chapter
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history/effective-date notes (effective 1-01-17). States that nothing in chapter 277 authorizes any private cause of action or establishes any "substitute principal of a law" (retaining archived source spelling "principal") in connection therewith. Separate review (antigravity_reviewer_r32): Retained drafted title after reading complete archived subsection text and notes. Verified verbatim archived phrase "substitute principal of a law" (spelled "principal") and 1-01-17 effective date; title avoids speculating beyond the clear no-private-cause-of-action clause.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived text of subsections 1–2 and history/effective-date notes (2014 S.B. 491 criminal-code revision, effective 1-01-17); verified all fingerprints. Confirmed class E felony for offering a bribe to livestock market/sale operators or market veterinarians and no-private-cause-of-action clause retaining verbatim archived wording "substitute principal of a law". Revised sub 1 title from "bribing" to "offering bribes to" to match exact statutory elements; retained sub 2 without speculating on the archived phrase.

headings.title: Law enforcement record inspections and livestock hold orders
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 including subdivisions (1)-(6) and continuation text in subdivision (6), plus history note (L. 2009 H.B. 62 § 1). Entitles law enforcement officers to inspect licensee records open under section 277.120 or to the department of agriculture during regular business hours without prior notice or warrant to determine livestock origin and destination, authorizes probable-cause hold orders on misappropriated livestock, lists six required contents, and mandates bilateral signatures/dates and a free executed copy. Separate review (antigravity_reviewer_r32): Retained drafted title after reading complete archived subsection text and notes.

headings.title: Definition of hold order
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note (L. 2009 H.B. 62 § 1). Defines "hold order" for section 277.190 as a written legal instrument issued by a law enforcement officer ordering a licensee to retain physical possession of livestock believed misappropriated for up to 24 hours without returning, selling, or disposing of it. Separate review (antigravity_reviewer_r32): Retained drafted title after reading complete archived subsection text and notes.

headings.title: Licensee duty to retain held livestock in secured area
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note (L. 2009 H.B. 62 § 1). Requires a licensee upon receiving a hold order to retain physical possession of the subject livestock in a secured area. Separate review (antigravity_reviewer_r32): Retained drafted title after reading complete archived subsection text and notes.

headings.title: Misdemeanor penalty, license sanctions, and appeals
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note (L. 2009 H.B. 62 § 1). Makes violation or noncompliance with section 277.190 a class A misdemeanor, makes gross negligence or willful noncompliance by a licensee grounds for license suspension or revocation, and permits appeal to the licensing authority or a court of competent jurisdiction. Separate review (antigravity_reviewer_r32): Retained drafted title after reading complete archived subsection text and notes.

headings.title: Confidentiality and permitted law enforcement uses of records
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 including subdivisions (1)-(2) and history note (L. 2009 H.B. 62 § 1). Makes licensee purchase and transaction records obtained under section 277.190 confidential and limits use exclusively to the appropriate law enforcement officer for investigating crimes involving the delivered livestock or notifying property crime victims where reported misappropriated livestock can be located. Separate review (antigravity_reviewer_r32): Retained drafted title after reading complete archived subsection text and notes.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived text of subsections 1–5 (including subdivisions (1)–(6) with continuation text in sub 1 and (1)–(2) in sub 5) and history note (L. 2009 H.B. 62 § 1); verified all fingerprints. Confirmed warrantless business-hours law enforcement inspection of section 277.120/department records, probable-cause 24-hour hold orders with 6 required fields and free signed copy, secured-area retention, class A misdemeanor/gross-negligence or willful license sanctions/appeals, and restricted confidential law enforcement use. All 5 drafted titles retained.
